record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the signature of the interaction matrix
record.statement: Let $M(\epsilon)$ be the matrix governing the stability of the graph-based gradient dynamics, with $\epsilon$ the interaction-strength parameter introduced above. The **signature monotonicity conjecture.** The signature of the matrix $M(\epsilon)$ is a monotonic decreasing function of $\epsilon$. Increasing $\epsilon$ is expected to make the adjacency-matrix contribution increasingly dominant and thereby increase the dimension of the unstable eigenspace; the conjecture concerns the resulting monotonicity of the matrix signature.

record.title: Ferroni–Matherne–Vecchi's real-rootedness conjecture for characteristic Chow polynomials
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite graded bounded poset, and let $P$ be Cohen–Macaulay. Denote by the characteristic Chow polynomial of $P$ the polynomial associated with $P$ in the Chow-polynomial construction. **Ferroni–Matherne–Vecchi's conjecture.** The characteristic Chow polynomial of $P$ is real-rooted. This extends the matroid Chow-polynomial real-rootedness conjecture to Cohen–Macaulay posets; the source does not give a resolution.

record.title: Vanishing multiplicities conjecture for degree-zero chromatic symmetric homology of star graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the star graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathcal{S}_\lambda$ be the Specht module indexed by a partition $\lambda$. Write $\lambda_2$ for the second part of $\lambda$, and let $H_{i,0}(G)$ denote the degree-zero chromatic symmetric homology component in homological degree $i$.

**Star-homology vanishing conjecture.** Whenever $i\ge 2$ or $\lambda_2\ge 3$, the multiplicity of $\mathcal{S}_\lambda$ in $H_{i,0}(G)$ is $0$.

The conjecture is presented as an essentially full description of the degree-zero chromatic symmetric homology for star graphs, beyond the separately identified exceptional summand $H_{0,0}(G)=\mathcal{S}_{1^n}$. No resolution is supplied in the excerpt.
record.source_name: Laura Pierson, “On the chromatic symmetric homology for star graphs”, arXiv:2408.01396 (2024).

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2024).

record.title: Robber strategies and non-principal single ultrafilters
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph or digraph inducing a connectivity system, and consider an elimination game with an invisible robber in which cop positions satisfy the relevant connectivity bound. **Robber-ultrafilter correspondence conjecture.** For suitable graph-induced connectivity systems, robber-winning strategies in elimination games are closely related to non-principal single ultrafilters. The supplied text presents this as a conjectural relationship without specifying the precise hypotheses or equivalence, so its formulation and consequences remain open.

record.title: Buchanan–odd-cover conjecture for complete graphs
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $b_2(G)$ denote its biclique partition number over the field of two elements, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. Let $k$ be a positive integer. **Buchanan–odd-cover conjecture.**

$$
b_2(K_{2k+1})=k+1,
$$

and

$$
b_2(K_{2k})=k+1
$$

whenever $k\equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ or $k\equiv 3 \pmod{4}$. This extends the known values for complete graphs in the odd-cover problem; the conjecture remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Calum Buchanan, Alexander Clifton, Eric Culver, Péter Frankl, Jiaxi Nie, Kenta Ozeki, Puck Rombach and Mei Yin, “On odd covers of cliques and disjoint unions”, arXiv:2408.08598 (2024).

record.title: Lonc–Elzobi's nice-property conjecture for products of chains
record.statement: For positive integers $n_1,\ldots,n_r$, let $\mathbf{n_i}$ denote a chain of length $n_i$, and let a lattice be **nice** when every stable-partition type dominates only types that are also realized by stable partitions. **Lonc–Elzobi's conjecture.** For any positive integers $n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_r$, the product $\mathbf{n_1}\times\mathbf{n_2}\times\cdots\times\mathbf{n_r}$ is nice. The source notes that Lonc and Elzobi proved the assertion for products of two chains, while the case of more than two chains is presented as an open problem.

record.title: Briggs's inequality for polynomials with only negative zeros
record.statement:
Let $f(x)=\sum_{l=0}^{n}a_lx^l$ be a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, and suppose that all zeros of $f(x)$ are negative. **Briggs's conjecture.** For $1\leq l\leq n-1$, one has

$$
a_{l-1}a_{l+2}^2+a_l^2a_{l+3}+a_{l+1}^3>a_{l+1}(a_{l-1}a_{l+3}+2a_la_{l+2}),
$$

and

$$
a_l^2(a_l^2-a_{l-1}a_{l+1})>a_{l-1}^2(a_{l+1}^2-a_la_{l+2}).
$$

The conjecture is the polynomial inequality underlying the Briggs inequalities studied for partition and overpartition functions; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Xin-Bei Liu and Zhong-Xue Zhang, “The Briggs inequality for partitions and overpartitions”, arXiv:2408.16185 (2024).

record.title: Facet- and vertex-minimality conjecture for the degree construction
record.statement:
Let $n$ be the dimension and let $k$ be the integer used in Theorem. Consider the triangulated $n$-sphere constructed there, together with its simplicial degree $k$ map to the standard triangulated sphere.

**Minimality conjecture.** The triangulated $n$-sphere constructed in Theorem is facet-minimal, and it is vertex-minimal as well.

The question concerns whether the construction gives optimal triangulations simultaneously with respect to the numbers of facets and vertices. The source presents this as a conjecture suggested by the facet-preimage behavior in the proof of the theorem; no resolution is given here.

record.title: The derangement-class product conjecture for finite simple transitive groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple transitive permutation group with point stabiliser $H$, and let $C,D$ be conjugacy classes of derangements in $G$. Set

$$
E(G,H)=\begin{cases}C^2\cup CD,&(G,H)=({\rm L}_2(7),S_4),\\\{1\}\cup CD,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

**Derangement-class product conjecture.** There exist conjugacy classes $C$ and $D$ of derangements such that

$$
G=E(G,H).
$$

This is proposed as a stronger form of the derangement-width conjecture. The paper proves the asserted form for alternating, sporadic and rank-one groups of Lie type, and for primitive groups with soluble point stabilisers; the general transitive case remains open.
record.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Marco Fusari, “On derangements in simple permutation groups”, arXiv:2409.01043 (2025).

record.title: The product-structure conjecture for k-independent crossing graphs
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. A graph is $k$-independent crossing if it has a topological drawing in which no edge is crossed by more than $k$ independent edges.

**Product-structure conjecture for $k$-independent crossing graphs.** The class of $k$-independent crossing graphs admits product structure.

This would extend the known product-structure results for planar and other beyond-planar graph classes. The paper applies the conjecture to canonical drawings of regular polygon intersection graphs, where bounded independent crossing is proved for $\alpha\geq s(n)$, but the general product-structure assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Laura Merker, Lena Scherzer, Samuel Schneider and Torsten Ueckerdt, “Intersection Graphs with and without Product Structure”, arXiv:2409.01732 (2024).

record.title: Generalized Lehman–Ron conjecture for directed hypercube layers
record.statement: Let $L_i$) and $L_j$ be layers of the directed hypercube, with $i<j$ and $r:=j-i$. Let $(S,T;\phi)$ be a matched pair with $S\subseteq L_i$ and $T\subseteq L_j$. **Generalized Lehman–Ron conjecture.** There are $r$ collections of vertex-disjoint paths between $S$ and $T$ such that their union is edge-disjoint. As the separation between the layers increases, the conjecture predicts proportionally more collections of paths; the paper states that its techniques do not resolve this claim.

record.title: Conjecture on the k-general position number of infinite grids
record.statement:
Let $P^{\Box,n}_\infty$ be the $n$-dimensional infinite grid, and let $\mathrm{gp}^k(G)$ denote its $k$-general position number. **Infinite-grid conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{gp}^k(P^{\Box,n}_\infty)=(k-1)^{2^{n-1}}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the preceding results on finite grids and by the known value for the relevant infinite-grid case. Its status and the range of parameters for which it remains open are not specified in the source.

record.title: Kaplan–Lev–Roditty's antimagic conjecture for trees
record.statement: Let $A$ be a finite Abelian group, and write $I(A)$ for the set of involutions of $A$. Set $A^*=A\setminus\{0\}$. An $A^*$-antimagic labeling of a graph with $|A|$ vertices is a bijection from its edges to $A^*$ such that all vertex sums are pairwise distinct. **Kaplan–Lev–Roditty's antimagic conjecture.** A tree with $|A|$ vertices is $A^*$-antimagic if and only if $|I(A)|\neq1$. The supplied source reports that this conjecture was proved for $4$-trees, but does not establish the full conjecture; the general assertion is therefore not resolved by the stated evidence.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, “E_A-cordial labeling of graphs and its implications for A-antimagic labeling of trees”, arXiv:2409.09136 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09136

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The tree antimagic conjecture for finite Abelian groups
record.statement: Let $A$ be a finite Abelian group, and let $T$ be a tree. An $A$-antimagic labeling is an edge labeling whose induced vertex sums are pairwise distinct. **Tree antimagic conjecture.** A tree $T$ is $A$-antimagic if and only if $|T|\not\equiv2\pmod 4$. This conjecture is motivated by the obstruction that no tree of order congruent to $2$ modulo $4$ admits an $A$-cordial labeling. The source presents the assertion as an open conjecture for trees in general.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, “E_A-cordial labeling of graphs and its implications for A-antimagic labeling of trees”, arXiv:2409.09136 (2024).

record.title: One-vaccination conjecture for the Pentagon Graph
record.statement: Let the Pentagon Graph be the infinite graph obtained from a pentagonal tiling of the plane, with vertices of degrees three and four. Consider the virus-containment process in which the outbreak starts from one infected vertex and one vaccination is placed at each time step. **The one-vaccination conjecture for the Pentagon Graph.** One vaccination per time step is not sufficient to control an outbreak on the Pentagon Graph. The claim extends the paper's investigation of containment protocols from regular infinite grids to this nonregular infinite graph; whether one vaccination per time step can ever contain an outbreak remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Alternating orientations minimize arborescences in Eulerian planar graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be an Eulerian planar graph. An orientation is **alternatingly in- and outward oriented at each vertex** when, in the cyclic order around every vertex, its incident edges alternate between incoming and outgoing; equivalently, each facial cycle is oriented. **Planar alternating-orientation conjecture.** The orientation minimizing the number of arborescences is the alternatingly in- and outward oriented orientation at each vertex, namely the orientation in which the cycle around each face is oriented. The conjecture is motivated by the relation between directed short cycles and arborescence numbers. In the planar dual formulation, it says that the standard orientation of the associated bipartite dual corresponds to a facet of minimal volume of the symmetric edge polytope.

record.title: The cubic graph list strong chromatic index conjecture at index five
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $\chi_s'(G)$ and $\chi_{s,l}'(G)$ denote its strong chromatic index and list strong chromatic index, respectively.

**Cubic index-five list-coloring conjecture.** If

$$
\chi_s'(G)=5,
$$

then

$$
\chi_{s,l}'(G)>5.
$$

The paper presents this as an expected extension of its infinite-family result. Whether every cubic graph with strong chromatic index $5$ has strictly larger list strong chromatic index remains open.
record.source_name: Borut Lužar, Edita Máčajová, Roman Soták and Diana Švecová, “List strong and list normal edge-coloring of (sub)cubic graphs”, arXiv:2410.01049 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01049

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “The conjecture was refuted in general by Kim and Park , but it is open for specific graph classes; for example, whether the two chromatic numbers are equal for the squares of line graphs.”

record.title: The edge-coloring conjecture for dual graphs of alcoved triangulations
record.statement:
Let $G=G_{\mathcal{A},i,d}$ and $H=G_{r,d}$. The edges of $G$ are colored according to the types of hyperplanes from the affine Coxeter arrangement of type $A_{d+1}$ to which they correspond. Let $G\langle H\rangle$ denote the graph obtained by using connecting sets between copies of $H$ indexed by the vertices of $G$.

**Edge-coloring conjecture.** The edge-coloring of $G$ determined by the hyperplane types prescribes a choice of connecting sets such that

$$
G\langle H\rangle
$$

is isomorphic to the dual graph of the alcoved triangulation of $r\Delta_{i,d}$.

The claim proposes that hyperplane-type edge-coloring supplies the compatibility needed in the graph construction. The source presents it as a proposed candidate, and no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Jerónimo Valencia-Porras, “A combinatorial proof of an identity involving Eulerian numbers”, arXiv:2410.01179 (2025).

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Gamma-positivity conjecture for dissonant canon polynomials
record.statement:
Let $P=[m]$, let $Q$ be a subposet of $P\times[n]$, and let $C^{Q,\operatorname{id}}(x)$ denote the dissonant canon polynomial associated with $Q$. **Gamma-positivity conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
C^{Q,\operatorname{id}}(x)
$$

is $\gamma$-positive whenever $P=[m]$. This conjecture arises from the question of which subposets yield $\gamma$-positive dissonant canon polynomials. The claim is known for canon permutations, corresponding to the poset $[m]\times[n]$, and for the poset corresponding to all multiset permutations; a unified interpretation of the $\gamma$-coefficients remains open for general subposets.
record.source_name: Matthias Beck and Danai Deligeorgaki, “Canon Permutation Posets”, arXiv:2410.03245 (2025).

record.title: Metric dimension formula for Villarceau grids
record.statement:
Let $VG^1_{m,n}$ and $VG^2_{m,n}$ be the two Villarceau grids, and let $\dim(G)$ denote the metric dimension of a graph $G$. For integers $m,n$ satisfying

$$
n>2m+1,
$$

**Metric dimension conjecture.**

$$
\dim(VG^1_{m,n})=\dim(VG^2_{m,n})=\left\lceil \frac{n-1}{m} \right\rceil+1.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the corresponding value for $VG^2_{m,n}$ when $n\leq 2m+1$; the displayed formula concerns the complementary range and is presented as a conjectural claim in the source.
record.source_name: S. Prabhu, D. Sagaya Rani Jeba, Paul Manuel and Akbar Davoodi, “Metric Dimension of Villarceau Grids”, arXiv:2410.08662 (2024).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2409.18914](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18914), [arXiv:2408.17229](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.17229).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08662
